definition: a plant with showy, intricately shaped flowers, often grown as a houseplant
modernAnchor: A delicate stem on a windowsill, a gift for a birthday or a wedding. We call it an orchid.
journey: Greek orkhis meant testicle, and the philosopher Theophrastus used it for a plant in his botany around 300 BCE.
The plant grew paired, rounded tubers underground, and to Greek eyes they looked anatomically familiar.
Ancient herbalists took the resemblance seriously, and orchid roots were eaten as a cure for fertility trouble.
In 1845 the botanist John Lindley anglicized the Latin orchis into orchid, and the blunt body part disappeared behind the flower.
